sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Mata seeks a court review of a board's denial of a deadline extension. Lynch argues the court lacks jurisdiction to review that specific denial.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Mata wants the Supreme Court to allow review of the board's extension denial.
Lynch wants the Supreme Court to confirm the lower court lacked jurisdiction to review the denial.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Mata argues the lower court made a fundamental administrative law error by recharacterizing the legal question.
Lynch argues the board's denial was a discretionary action that courts cannot review.

paragraphs: Justice Scalia asked why the Fifth Circuit treated the extension denial as a sua sponte action.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the scope of judicial review over agency deadline extensions. It determines whether courts can correct legal errors in agency scheduling decisions. The outcome shapes the balance between agency discretion and judicial oversight.
